title: We Long to See That Happy Time
description: We Long to See That Happy Time in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 310 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Gospel Freedom Universal”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: We long to see that hap-py time, That long ex-pect-ed, bliss-ful day, When men of ev-ery name and clime The glo-rious gos-pel shall o-bey.

lines: We long to see that happy time,
When men of every name and clime
The word of God shall firm abide,
Though earth and hell should dare oppose;
The stone cut from the mountain's side,
Shall shout to Asia's rapt'rous song,
And western climes the strain prolong.
From east to west, from north to south,
And every man, in every face,
Shall meet a brother and a friend.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
